## Verdict: PASS

N-56 (5)'s kernel part is fixed (section 1). Every gate exits 0 (section 2). NEAR is green, and RELATED at 1000 has no
red that belongs to the item (section 2). There is no behaviour shift: on 1 800 probe steps, the s4 line and the s5 line
gave byte-identical arena bits, commit records and level digests.

Of 11 targeted mutants, 10 were killed by the item's own `savepoint.test.ts`. One (M04) survives and is equivalent for
the key. One new finding is not a blocker: out-of-LIFO image use can collide keys (N-24). No M0 path reaches it, so it
is a hardening note and does not fail the item. That classification is vetoable.

## 1. The round's failing line, re-run

| line | evidence re-run by this seat | verdict | label |
|---|---|---|---|
| **N-56 (5) Q28 (kernel part).** `restoreSavepoint` across committed batches sets `p.version` back, so a maintained level-digest state can read current with stale digests. The kernel must expose a restore generation. | **The code.** I diffed against the s4 line, the ruling mirror's `src/tx/savepoint.ts` and `index.ts`. The only executable change is `savepoint.ts:155` `const RESTORES = new WeakMap<Plat, number>();`, `:162–164` `restoreGeneration(p)` returning `RESTORES.get(p) ?? 0`, and `:173` `if (p.version !== s.version) RESTORES.set(p, restoreGeneration(p) + 1);`. Line 173 sits before `p.version = s.version`. The rest is doc lines. `tx/index.ts:57` exports `restoreGeneration`, and `src/index.ts:11` (`export * from './tx/index.js'`) carries it to `@plat/kernel`. No `Plat` field was added and no persisted format changed. `p.version` is written only by `commitVersion` (`arena/plat.ts:729`), `restoreSavepoint` and `io/compact.ts:176` (a new arena object, generation 0). Every in-batch restore is at the batch's own version: `tx.ts:136` `reject`, `:562` the throw path, `:612` the no-op commit, and `faces/common.ts:510` the op rollback. `commitVersion` runs only after every check (`tx.ts:650`), and a throw from `onCommit` comes after `t.closed = true`, so nothing is restored then. **Reproduce, then clear** (`zz-check-s5.test.ts`, `out/probe.txt`). With the ruling's scenario as written (digest keyed on the version only, which M0-d-04's round s1 has yet to change), it is still stale: `n=3 m=3 bare {"stale":true,"builds":1,"version":4,"versionSeen":4,"gen":1,…,"perLevel":[true,false,false,false,false]}` and `n=1 m=1 … "stale":true … "gen":1`. A consumer that re-attaches when `restoreGeneration` differs from its value at attach reads current in every shape: `n=1 m=1`, `n=3 m=3`, `n=3 m=2` and `n=3 m=4` all give `keyed {"stale":false,…}`. **The key's promise.** In 600 random LIFO sequences of 40 steps (nested take, restore and drop up to depth 3; commits at L1 and L2; refused callbacks, throws and empty batches), the probe made 727 cross-commit restores, 1 339 same-version restores, 7 426 refused or rejected batches and 5 835 distinct keys. No (generation, version) key named two contents, and the generation always equalled the probe's own count of cross-commit restores, kept from commit counts and not from `p.version` (`maxGen 5`; `Tests 3 passed (3)`). **Pins** (`savepoint.test.ts`, describe `N-56 (5)`, six tests). They cover: the export through `@plat/kernel` and 0 after commits; a cross-commit restore bumping by exactly one at n = 1 and 3, and a same-version restore not bumping; n rolled back and n replayed reaching the same version with the generation one higher; the generation surviving four commits and a second cross-commit restore bumping to 2; 20 rejected batches (refused callback, `E_WORK_LIMIT` callback, a throw, `E_WORK_LIMIT` declared, empty) bumping nothing, with `state(p)` unchanged and version 1; and per-arena independence. `9 passed (9)` in the file. **Mutants** (section 3): bump on every restore, never bump, and compare after the version is set back are all KILLED by these pins. **C-0299** records the export as one more public export under J248's class, vetoable. | fixed | CONFIRMED |

## 4. New findings (none a blocker)

* **N-24 (notes).** Out-of-LIFO use breaks the doc's claim that "(generation, version) is never reached twice with
  different content". The case is a dead image, one taken before a restore to an older image, put back later at an
  equal version. CONFIRMED: `nonLIFO k1 1:3 k2 1:3 sameKey true sameContent false`, and a (generation, version)-keyed
  consumer then reads L1–L4 stale. On 300 random out-of-LIFO sequences there were 143 collisions in 48 sequences, and
  60 restores threw a `TypeError` in `restoreIndex` (`savepoint.ts:92`). No M0 path reaches it: the runner uses one
  image per stage (`runner.ts:330`, `rollBack`), and batches restore at their own version. So it is a contrived-use
  escape (N-45), not a wrong result on an honest input. It is recorded for the hardening phase with N-23: either refuse
  a dead image, or bump on a generation mismatch stored in the image.
* **N-25 (notes).** M04 is equivalent, as argued above. Pinning this seat's LIFO property in `savepoint.test.ts` is a
  hardening test.
* C-0299 (5)'s note on `geom/neighbours.ts` `keptMap` and `arena/resolve.ts` `isCurrent`/`assertStamp` is other items'
  business and is already reported to the session; this seat adds nothing to it.
